# Issue #359: Propose public lineage adjudication rules and apply them to the 13 version-difference candidate groups (gap delta #330 N2)

## Goal
benchmark/lineage.json holds 230 `candidate_variants` groups (rule same-basename, reason different-sha256), all `candidate-unadjudicated`. Gap delta #330 lists N2 (public lineage adjudication) as now-doable. 13 groups have a version difference. Write adjudication rules and apply them to those 13 groups as a pilot. Report only: do not edit repository files (lineage.json is pinned).

Expected gain: tested rules that a later Policymaker landing script can apply to all 230 groups, so public lineage stops being unadjudicated. The next Policymaker reads the rule list and a JSON block with one decision per pilot group in this report.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Write `.session/report.md` in your first turns and update it.
- [ ] Rules: a small set of labels (for example same-lineage, independent, undecidable), each with the static evidence it needs (member paths, repository, save version, XML or binary name evidence). Hash inequality alone never proves independence (benchmark/lineage.md). Undecidable stays a visible gap.
- [ ] Select the 13 groups by script from lineage.json (version difference in `recorded_save_versions`). For each give: candidate id, label, evidence pointers (artifact ids, paths, file offsets or lines), and the rule used.
- [ ] One fenced ```json block with `{"rules": [...], "decisions": [...]}` so a script can extract it. Give the sha256 of lineage.json you read.
- [ ] State how long the full 230 groups would take with the same rules (measured per-group cost).

## Verification
`python3 -I -B policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`

## Context
- benchmark/lineage.md and benchmark/lineage.json (`candidate_variants`, `artifacts`).
- benchmark/scripts/lineage.py: how candidates were formed (needs LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT for originals).

## Budget
- At most 25 tool calls, under 300k input tokens. Read lineage.json only through bounded python3 -I queries, never whole. Do not read benchmark/cases or benchmark/results bodies.

# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
The existing evaluator verifier supplies the independent readiness checks, in another session.

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a sha256 for each evidence file. After rebase the engine
runs `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` and rejects the session when a pinned
file changed without its hash (session #117 was lost this way). Whenever you change a file
listed there, or add evidence for a milestone, rewrite its `sha256` in the same change and
run that check yourself (exit 0 required; it needs no LabVIEW environment). Each evidence
file must stay under 2 MB. If `git commit` fails for a missing identity, leave the changes
staged and say so; the engine commits accepted changes.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Inventory public copies and possible variants, using only the standard library.
Run with python3 -I. Prepared source code is never imported or executed.
All pinned inputs and original/member bytes are checked before any output write.
"""
import argparse
from collections import defaultdict
import hashlib
import io
import itertools
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import posixpath
import subprocess
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import zipfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
GROUP_PREFIX = 'public-repository-'
MISSING = ['restricted store', 'custodian', 'private/new cases',
           'native structural comparison', 'tested isolation']
def split_text(split):
    reference = " (benchmark/split/, review #273)" if split == "design-reviewed" else ""
    return "Split is " + split + reference + "; no evaluation partitions are allocated."


def limitation(split):
    detail = (
        " Split is a reviewed design only (benchmark/split/ with benchmark/scripts/split_boundary.py, "
        "review #273 accept, the two non-blocking checker findings of #273 were fixed by #281 "
        "(not independently re-reviewed)): no allocation exists, no isolation step is executed, "
        "the restricted store (capability #268) is not ready, and no secrecy is claimed; "
        "author (copilot gpt-5.6-luna) and reviewer (codex gpt-6.1-sol) are both GPT-family models."
    ) if split == "design-reviewed" else ""
    return ("Public lineage inventory is prepared, unreviewed preparation only. "
            + split_text(split) + detail + " Still missing: " + ", ".join(MISSING)
            + ". Hash inequality does not establish independence. No evaluation allocation or readiness claim.")


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def encode(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n').encode('utf-8')


def safe_path(relative):
    require(isinstance(relative, str) and relative and '\\' not in relative,
            'Invalid relative path')
    path = PurePosixPath(relative)
    require(not path.is_absolute() and '..' not in path.parts and str(path) == relative,
            'Unsafe/noncanonical path: ' + relative)
    return path


def read_regular(base, relative):
    path = safe_path(relative)
    current = base
    require(not current.is_symlink(), 'Symlink root: ' + str(base))
    for part in path.parts:
        current = current / part
        require(not current.is_symlink(), 'Symlink: ' + str(current))
    require(current.is_file(), 'Missing regular file: ' + str(current))
    return current.read_bytes()


def git_head(directory):
    result = subprocess.run([
        'git', '--no-replace-objects', '--no-optional-locks',
        '-c', 'safe.directory=' + str(directory), '-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false',
        '-C', str(directory), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, check=False)
    require(result.returncode == 0, 'Cannot inspect prepared Git HEAD')
    return result.stdout.decode('ascii').strip()


def pinned_inputs():
    preparation = json.loads(read_regular(ROOT, 'benchmark/preparation.json'))
    pins = defaultdict(set)
    for entries in preparation['milestones'].values():
        for entry in entries:
            pins[entry['path']].add(entry['sha256'])
    paths = ['benchmark/sources.json', 'benchmark/coverage.json',
             'benchmark/preparation-status.json']
    paths += sorted(str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) for p in
                    (ROOT / 'benchmark/cases/dev').glob('*.json'))
    require(len(paths) > 3, 'No development cases')
    contents = {}
    for path in paths:
        data = read_regular(ROOT, path)
        require(pins[path] == {sha(data)}, 'Missing/conflicting/stale input pin: ' + path)
        contents[path] = data
    sources = json.loads(contents['benchmark/sources.json'])
    coverage = json.loads(contents['benchmark/coverage.json'])
    require(coverage['sources_json_sha256'] == sha(contents['benchmark/sources.json']),
            'Coverage was generated from different sources')
    status = json.loads(contents['benchmark/preparation-status.json'])
    require(status['milestones']['split'] in ('not-started', 'design-reviewed'),
            'Unexpected split status')
    return preparation, contents, sources, coverage, status


def inventory(environment, sources, coverage):
    repositories = {r['name']: r for r in sources['repositories']}
    require(len(repositories) == len(sources['repositories']), 'Duplicate repository name')
    for name, repository in sorted(repositories.items()):
        safe_path(name)
        require('/' not in name, 'Invalid repository name')
        require(git_head(environment / name) == repository['commit'], 'Prepared commit mismatch: ' + name)
    require(sha(read_regular(environment, 'readiness.json')) == sources['preparation_readiness_sha256'],
            'Prepared readiness hash mismatch')
    originals = {}
    for name, repository in sorted(repositories.items()):
        for artifact in repository['artifacts']:
            path = name + '/' + artifact['path']
            data = read_regular(environment, path)
            require(sha(data) == artifact['sha256'] and len(data) == artifact['size'],
                    'Source original mismatch: ' + path)
            require(path not in originals, 'Duplicate source original: ' + path)
            originals[path] = data
    records = {}
    for artifact in coverage['artifacts']:
        archive = artifact['archive']
        path = artifact['path']
        safe_path(path)
        if archive is None:
            repository, relative = path.split('/', 1)
            require(repository in repositories, 'Unknown coverage repository')
            data = originals.get(path)
            if data is None:
                data = read_regular(environment, path)
            originals[path] = data
            key = (repository, '', relative, -1)
        else:
            safe_path(archive)
            repository = archive.split('/', 1)[0]
            require(repository in repositories, 'Unknown archive repository')
            index = artifact['member_index']
            require(type(index) is int and index >= 0, 'Invalid archive member index')
            key = (repository, archive, path, index)
            data = None
        require(key not in records, 'Duplicate coverage location')
        records[key] = (artifact, data)
    disk_paths = {k[0] + '/' + k[2] for k in records if not k[1]}
    require(set(originals) <= disk_paths, 'Source original missing from coverage denominator')
    disk_pins = {k[0] + '/' + k[2]: a for k, (a, _) in records.items() if not k[1]}
    for path, data in originals.items():
        require(sha(data) == disk_pins[path]['sha256'] and len(data) == disk_pins[path]['size'],
                'Coverage original mismatch: ' + path)
    archives = {}
    for key, (artifact, data) in list(records.items()):
        if key[1]:
            archive = key[1]
            require(archive in disk_pins, 'Unpinned archive container: ' + archive)
            if archive not in archives:
                archives[archive] = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(originals[archive]))
            handle = archives[archive]
            entries = handle.infolist()
            require(key[3] < len(entries), 'Missing member index')
            info = entries[key[3]]
            require(info.filename == key[2] and not info.is_dir(), 'Archive member identity mismatch')
            require(info.file_size == artifact['size'], 'Archive member size mismatch')
            data = handle.read(info)
            records[key] = (artifact, data)
        require(sha(data) == artifact['sha256'] and len(data) == artifact['size'],
                'Coverage member/original hash mismatch: ' + str(key))
    for handle in archives.values():
        handle.close()
    artifacts = []
    payloads = {}
    for index, (key, (artifact, data)) in enumerate(sorted(records.items())):
        repository, archive, path, member_index = key
        item = {
            'id': 'artifact-%04d' % index, 'repository': repository,
            'path': path, 'archive': archive or None,
            'member_index': member_index if archive else None,
            'sha256': artifact['sha256'], 'size': artifact['size'],
            'family': artifact['family'], 'save_versions': artifact['save_versions'],
            'declared_qualified_names': [],
        }
        if archive:
            item['container_sha256'] = disk_pins[archive]['sha256']
        artifacts.append(item)
        payloads[item['id']] = data
    require(len(artifacts) == coverage['denominator']['artifact_entries'], 'Coverage count mismatch')
    return artifacts, payloads, repositories


def declared_names(artifacts, payloads):
    """Static XML membership clues, never a native name/structural assertion."""
    locations = defaultdict(list)
    for item in artifacts:
        locations[(item['repository'], item['archive'], item['path'])].append(item['id'])
    by_id = {item['id']: item for item in artifacts}
    parents = defaultdict(set)
    declarations = []
    containers = set()
    gaps = []
    for item in artifacts:
        if PurePosixPath(item['path']).suffix.lower() not in ('.lvlib', '.lvclass'):
            continue
        try:
            root = ET.fromstring(payloads[item['id']])
        except ET.ParseError:
            gaps.append({'artifact': item['id'], 'reason': 'Container is not parseable XML'})
            continue
        containers.add(item['id'])
        for ordinal, member in enumerate(root.iter('Item')):
            url = member.get('URL', '')
            name = member.get('Name', '')
            if not url or not name:
                continue
            # LabVIEW symbolic/absolute URLs require native resolution; retain the gap.
            if url.startswith('/') or ':' in url or '\\' in url:
                gaps.append({'artifact': item['id'], 'item_ordinal': ordinal,
                             'reason': 'Nonrelative membership URL not resolved'})
                continue
            # These serialized URLs traverse from the container path itself.
            # Parent/friend references express relationships, not ownership.
            if member.get('Type') in ('Parent', 'Friended VI', 'Class Private Data'):
                gaps.append({'artifact': item['id'], 'item_ordinal': ordinal,
                             'reason': 'Nonownership or implicit private-data declaration excluded from name inference'})
                continue
            target = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(item['path'], url))
            if target.startswith('../'):
                gaps.append({'artifact': item['id'], 'item_ordinal': ordinal,
                             'reason': 'Membership URL escapes inventory root'})
                continue
            matches = locations.get((item['repository'], item['archive'], target), [])
            if not matches:
                gaps.append({'artifact': item['id'], 'item_ordinal': ordinal,
                             'reason': 'Membership URL target absent from pinned inventory'})
            for target_id in matches:
                parents[target_id].add((item['id'], name))
                declarations.append({'container': item['id'], 'item_ordinal': ordinal,
                                     'name': name, 'url': url, 'target': target_id})
    def names(identity, visited):
        if identity in visited:
            return set()
        result = set()
        for parent, name in sorted(parents[identity]):
            for prefix in names(parent, visited | {identity}):
                result.add(prefix + ':' + name)
        if not parents[identity] and identity in containers:
            result.add(PurePosixPath(by_id[identity]['path']).name)
        return result
    for item in artifacts:
        item['declared_qualified_names'] = sorted(names(item['id'], set()))
    return declarations, gaps


def group_candidates(artifacts):
    buckets = defaultdict(list)
    for item in artifacts:
        buckets[('same-relative-name', item['path'])].append(item)
        for name in item['declared_qualified_names']:
            buckets[('same-declared-qualified-name', name)].append(item)
        # Additional conservative clue for moved/binary files whose native names are unavailable.
        buckets[('same-basename', PurePosixPath(item['path']).name)].append(item)
    candidates = []
    pairs = set()
    for (rule, name), members in sorted(buckets.items()):
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        hashes = {m['sha256'] for m in members}
        versions = {v['decoded'] for m in members for v in m['save_versions']
                    if v.get('decoded') and v['field'] in ('LVSR', 'XML root @LVVersion')}
        if len(hashes) < 2 and len(versions) < 2:
            continue
        reasons = ['different-sha256'] if len(hashes) > 1 else []
        if len(versions) > 1:
            reasons.append('different-recorded-save-versions')
        ids = sorted(m['id'] for m in members)
        candidates.append({'id': 'candidate-%04d' % len(candidates),
                           'status': 'candidate-unadjudicated', 'rule': rule,
                           'matching_name': name, 'reasons': reasons,
                           'distinct_hashes': len(hashes), 'recorded_save_versions': sorted(versions),
                           'members': ids})
        pairs.update(tuple(sorted((a['id'], b['id']))) for a, b in itertools.combinations(members, 2)
                     if a['sha256'] != b['sha256'])
    return candidates, len(pairs)


def lineage_map(artifacts, exact, candidates, cases, repositories):
    by_id = {a['id']: a for a in artifacts}
    joins = {name: {name} for name in repositories}
    for group in exact + candidates:
        names = {by_id[identity]['repository'] for identity in group['members']}
        for name in names:
            joins[name].update(names)
    for name in sorted(joins):
        frontier = list(joins[name])
        while frontier:
            other = frontier.pop()
            new = joins[other] - joins[name]
            joins[name].update(new)
            frontier.extend(new)
    mapped = defaultdict(list)
    case_records = []
    dev_repositories = defaultdict(set)
    for path, data in sorted(cases.items()):
        case = json.loads(data)
        original = case['artifact']
        repository = original['repository']
        require(repository in repositories and original['commit'] == repositories[repository]['commit'],
                'Development repository pin mismatch: ' + path)
        require(original['identity_manifest_sha256'] == sha(read_regular(ROOT, original['identity_manifest'])),
                'Development identity manifest changed: ' + path)
        chain = original['archive_member_chain']
        require(len(chain) <= 1, 'Nested development archive requires explicit support')
        archive = repository + '/' + chain[0]['container_path'] if chain else None
        matches = [a for a in artifacts if a['repository'] == repository and
                   a['path'] == original['path'] and a['archive'] == archive and
                   a['sha256'] == original['sha256'] and
                   (not chain or (a['member_index'] == chain[0]['member_index'] and
                                  a['container_sha256'] == chain[0]['container_sha256'] and
                                  a['sha256'] == chain[0]['member_sha256'] and
                                  a['path'] == chain[0]['member_path']))]
        require(len(matches) == 1, 'Development artifact does not resolve uniquely: ' + path)
        group = case['lineage_group_id']
        require(isinstance(group, str) and group, 'Missing development lineage ID')
        dev_repositories[group].add(repository)
        case_records.append({'path': path, 'sha256': sha(data), 'lineage_group_id': group,
                             'artifact_id': matches[0]['id']})
    groups = {}
    for group, names in sorted(dev_repositories.items()):
        closure = set().union(*(joins[name] for name in names))
        mapped[group] = [a['id'] for a in artifacts if a['repository'] in closure]
        groups[group] = {'members': mapped[group], 'repositories': sorted(closure),
                         'status': 'conservative-public-development-constraint',
                         'method': 'Whole repositories plus cross-repository exact/candidate closure; preserves existing dev lineage IDs.'}
    for name in sorted(repositories):
        if not any(name in g['repositories'] for g in groups.values()):
            closure = joins[name]
            group = GROUP_PREFIX + '-and-'.join(sorted(closure))
            groups[group] = {'members': [a['id'] for a in artifacts if a['repository'] in closure],
                             'repositories': sorted(closure), 'status': 'provisional-public-project-envelope',
                             'method': 'Conservative whole-repository envelope; absence of matches is not independence.'}
    for case in case_records:
        require(case['artifact_id'] in groups[case['lineage_group_id']]['members'], 'Dev lineage disagreement')
    return groups, case_records


def build():
    preparation, contents, sources, coverage, status = pinned_inputs()
    environment_value = os.environ.get('LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT')
    require(environment_value, 'LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT is required')
    environment = Path(environment_value)
    require(environment.is_absolute() and environment.is_dir(), 'Invalid LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT')
    artifacts, payloads, repositories = inventory(environment, sources, coverage)
    declarations, name_gaps = declared_names(artifacts, payloads)
    hashes = defaultdict(list)
    for artifact in artifacts:
        hashes[artifact['sha256']].append(artifact['id'])
    exact = [{'sha256': digest, 'members': members} for digest, members in sorted(hashes.items())]
    candidates, pair_count = group_candidates(artifacts)
    cases = {p: d for p, d in contents.items() if p.startswith('benchmark/cases/dev/')}
    groups, case_records = lineage_map(artifacts, exact, candidates, cases, repositories)
    duplicate = [g for g in exact if len(g['members']) > 1]
    counts = {'repositories': len(repositories), 'artifacts': len(artifacts),
              'originals': sum(a['archive'] is None for a in artifacts),
              'archive_members': sum(a['archive'] is not None for a in artifacts),
              'exact_hash_groups_including_singletons': len(exact),
              'exact_duplicate_groups': len(duplicate),
              'exact_duplicate_members': sum(len(g['members']) for g in duplicate),
              'candidate_groups': len(candidates), 'distinct_different_hash_candidate_pairs': pair_count,
              'candidate_groups_with_version_difference': sum('different-recorded-save-versions' in c['reasons'] for c in candidates),
              'conservative_lineage_groups': len(groups), 'development_cases': len(case_records),
              'development_lineage_ids': len({c['lineage_group_id'] for c in case_records}),
              'static_membership_declarations': len(declarations), 'static_name_gaps': len(name_gaps)}
    result = {'schema_version': 1, 'scope': 'Public development sources only; no allocation into evaluation partitions.',
              'status': 'prepared-unreviewed', 'split_milestone': status['milestones']['split'],
              'input_pins': {p: sha(d) for p, d in sorted(contents.items()) if not p.endswith('preparation-status.json')},

# Ocena początkowa i droga do benchmarku

Stan startowy: **skuteczność narzędzia niezmierzona, benchmark nie istnieje**.
Temat setupu przygotowuje ocenę; nie buduje produktu ani docelowego zestawu przypadków.
Podstawą są ustalenia [niezależnej weryfikacji](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/10#issuecomment-6225343449)
i [dostępu do środowiska](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
Kompilacja przykładu VI z 2014 w kontenerze NI 2026 Q1 dowodzi dostępu do tego środowiska,
nie poprawności czytnika, VI Scripting ani obsługi wszystkich wersji. Dostęp 2024 pozostaje niezweryfikowany.

## Co rozstrzyga skrypt, a co właściciel

Zachowano dostarczoną bramkę `gate.kind: owner`. Każda zmiana pracy czeka na decyzję
właściciela; nie zaakceptowano progów jakości ani samodzielnego kończenia celu.
Właściciel ocenia treść dowodów, dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej
metodzie weryfikacji, akceptuje progi sukcesu i ewentualną zmianę zakresu. W temacie D
zaakceptował zasady sukcesu zapisane w `goal/goal.md`: pełny zakres, osobne pomiary
wierności odczytu i odpowiedzi popartych źródłem oraz niezależny benchmark z porównaniem.
Progi jakości i wykonywalna bramka celu czekają na wiarygodny benchmark i osobną
akceptację właściciela; przyszła bramka wymaga `owner_confirms: true`. Plik
`goal/gate.yml` pozostaje nieobecny, więc pętla nie ogłasza samodzielnie sukcesu. Zastąpienie
bramki skryptem wymaga jego decyzji oraz niezależnie sprawdzonej metody. Nie jest to
ograniczenie celu do wersji lub rodzin obecnych w pierwszych przykładach.

`check` uruchamia `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` w kandydacie. Sprawdza
jedynie poprawność opcjonalnego indeksu dowodów: schemat, lokalne ścieżki, niepuste pliki
i SHA256. Brak indeksu jest normalnym stanem początkowym, raportowanym jawnie; błędny
istniejący indeks zatrzymuje zmianę. Ten check nie potwierdza treści dokumentów ani jakości.
Nie wykonuje kodu wskazanego w dowodach. Testy tego skryptu i silnika nie są benchmarkiem LabVIEW.

Raport porównawczy uruchamia się z **zaakceptowanego drzewa**, podając oba katalogi:

```sh
python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --baseline /accepted --candidate /candidate
```

Obsługiwane są też `BASELINE_DIR` i `CANDIDATE_DIR`. Ostatnia linia to JSON zgodny z
kontraktem silnika. Raport zawiera oba stany; błędne dowody kandydata dają `rejected`,
pozostałe przypadki `inconclusive`, zawsze `improved: false`. Nawet komplet odnośników
nie oznacza gotowości benchmarku. `tool_quality: null`, `benchmark_executed: false` oraz
`benchmark_ready: false` pozostają jawne. Raport jest pomocą dla właściciela; przy bramce
`owner` silnik nie uruchamia go automatycznie i nie wykorzystuje go do automatycznego przyjęcia.
Brak pomiaru pozostaje brakiem pomiaru, także po usunięciu lub wymianie indeksu.

Indeks `benchmark/preparation.json` powstanie podczas pracy pętli. Wzór, nie gotowy benchmark:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"milestones":{"sources":[],"tasks":[],"oracle":[],"split":[],"coverage":[],"baseline":[],"challenges":[]}}
```

Każda lista zawiera wpisy `{"path":"benchmark/protocol.md","sha256":"<64 znaki SHA256>"}`.
Dowody muszą być plikami w drzewie, bez symlinków, do 2 MB każdy; duże dane opisuje mały
rekord z przypiętym źródłem i hashem. Sekcje i liczba odnośników służą nawigacji, nie punktacji.
Check działa tylko dla zmian pracy; ścieżki polityki/audytu/dziennika omijają go zgodnie
z silnikiem. Weryfikator sam uruchamia testy każdej zmiany evaluatora.

## Co musi powstać przed implementacją

Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.

| Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
|---|---|
| sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
| tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
| oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
| split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
| coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
| baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
| challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |

Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.

Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.

## Niezależna kontrola zmian

Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja
obowiązuje do wyniku `pass`; zmieniony snapshot wymaga ponownej kontroli.
Instrukcje weryfikatora, wspólny kontrakt roli i protokół są chronione w `engine.yml`.
Silnik blokuje też zmianę/usunięcie wpisu `evaluator-verifier` w profilach, zachowując
możliwość tworzenia pozostałych ról. Zmiana tych zabezpieczeń należy do właściciela.
Niezależność oznacza osobną sesję i dowody, nie gwarancję bezbłędności modelu; przy
niepewności weryfikator odmawia `pass`. To nie bramka końcowego sukcesu; jej odroczenie
i wymagane potwierdzenie właściciela zapisano w `goal/goal.md` w temacie D.

Stworzyć narzędzie, które pozwoli agentom AI czytać kod, projekty i wszystkie artefakty LabVIEW tak samo jak zwykły kod.

Przed implementacją narzędzia opracować wiarygodny benchmark lub inną powtarzalną metodę weryfikacji, która pozwoli sprawdzić, czy narzędzie działa.

Właściciel zaakceptował następujące zasady:

- Osobno sprawdzać wierność odczytu artefaktów oraz poprawność odpowiedzi agenta i ich poparcie wskazaniem źródła w oryginalnym artefakcie.

# Environment readiness

The owner requires the entire loop to execute in the cloud. Their Windows machine
is not a runner. Public source preparation and model access checks run on GitHub
hosted Ubuntu. Official NI headless automation is now verified in the cloud;
interactive IDE access is not part of this setup path.
The product goal is unchanged and no artifact family has been excluded.

Version requirement clarified by the owner on 18 October 2026: prioritize all
LabVIEW versions; LabVIEW 2024 is the accepted fallback if investigation shows
substantially greater time is needed for all versions. Estimate that difference
before choosing a version scope. No numeric time threshold was agreed. The local
LabVIEW 2026 observation does not verify LabVIEW 2024 or cross-version compatibility.

## Reproducible public sources

`policy/prepare.sh` calls `.github/loop/prepare_environment.py` from the session's checkout. It needs Python 3.10+
and git, no secrets, pip installations or NI activation. Sources and exact commits
are in `.github/loop/environment-sources.json`:

- NI Actor Framework, MIT, commit `371c631c16155d88f02be11a953e4964d7452fd8`.
- pylavi, Unlicense, commit `35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75`.

The check fetches these commits, rejects tracked modifications in its cache,
checks license markers and the SHA256 of one real NI VI, loads its resource table
with the pinned parser, and parses a real LabVIEW project as XML. It writes
`readiness.json` and exposes the cache as `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` to subsequent job
steps. Default cache: `$RUNNER_TEMP/connectwithlabview-environment`.
Public copies stay outside git. No NI installation files or personal projects are
redistributed. Downloads require outbound HTTPS to GitHub.

Preparation passed twice in a clean Linux Python 3.12 container and on Windows
Python 3.14. The checked VI contains 30 resource types; this is evidence of resource
access, not correctness of diagram interpretation. The public project reports
LVVersion `20008000`. Broader coverage and independent expected answers belong to
the evaluator/benchmark work; do not use parser output as its own sole oracle.

Hosted confirmation: [Environment readiness, run 39073653443](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/actions/runs/39073653443)
on 18 October 2026 (Europe/Warsaw) passed public source preparation and its second
invocation on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04.

The engine test suite passed on Linux/Python 3.12: 263 tests, 11 skipped
(template-only and opt-in live checks). This includes the routing and probe
classification tests. It does not validate unfinished adapter integration.

## Cloud provider access checks

`.github/workflows/environment.yml` runs on setup-branch changes to environment
code, and can be dispatched after GitHub registers the workflow. It does not call
the loop, merge work, or enable `AUTOPILOT`. Repository Actions are enabled; the
provider jobs need `contents: read` plus their provider permissions. Setup proof
jobs additionally need `contents: write` for separate task refs, state and
checkpoint assets; they do not merge to the default branch. No custom
runner is registered. `AUTOPILOT=off` is explicit during setup.

Pinned CLI packages are recorded in `.github/loop/cloud-providers.json`. Each
provider job installs just its CLI, calls a fixed probe in an isolated temporary
home, and uploads a summary, never credentials or raw model streams. A missing
secret, exhausted quota or failed response fails that readiness check. Generic
429/network failures remain unknown; they do not prove a depleted subscription.

| Provider | Repository secret | Access semantics |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | The owner created a supported long-lived token with `claude setup-token` and replaced the secret on 18 October 2026. Hosted probes reach the service but report subscription exhaustion. Track eventual replacement in the credential lifecycle. |
| Codex | Maintenance environment `CODEX_CI_AUTH_JSON`; execution `CODEX_WORKER_AUTH_JSON` | The owner provisioned the dedicated CI login and scoped App. Sequential cloud runners verified forced renewal and write-back; workers receive only access tokens. |
| Copilot | Job `GITHUB_TOKEN`, passed as `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | The readiness job now requests `copilot-requests: write` and checks the pinned CLI. Current GitHub documentation supports this in personally owned repositories against the owner's seat. The earlier copied OAuth token remains stored but is no longer passed by this readiness job. |

The owner requested access to these accounts for cloud execution. Bootstrap values
were transferred directly to encrypted repository secrets without printing them.
They are not a complete unattended credential-renewal system. No API billing mode,
automatic credit purchase or provider substitution has been enabled.

The [credential requirements and accepted public repository](cloud-authentication.md)
record verified renewal requirements and cloud evidence. The owner explicitly
retained this public repository on 18 October 2026 and rejected a private control
repository. OpenAI's account-auth CI deployment recommendation covers private
automation; that recommendation does not cover the chosen layout. Trusted workflow
and credential-isolation checks must replace that assumption. No visibility or
billing change has been made.

Local diagnostic observations before adopting the cloud-only constraint: Claude
2.1.292 was authenticated but its real call reported a weekly subscription limit,
reset 20 October 2026 at 21:00 Europe/Warsaw. Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 and Copilot
1.0.98 returned their expected probe answers. Those local observations do not by
themselves prove cloud access. The hosted workflow's summaries are the cloud evidence.

That hosted run returned `available` with an actual model answer for Codex and
Copilot, and `quota` for Claude. The overall run therefore correctly failed
readiness. Claude's cloud call reached the service and reported a subscription
limit; it did not produce a usable model answer. These observations are point-in-time
checks, not promises of availability or durable token renewal.

## Required multi-provider execution

The owner accepted [Cloud model selection and quota management](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/11).
The existing engine still launches Claude. Installing the other CLIs does not
integrate task execution, stream accounting, permissions or the watchdog.

`provider_pool.py` is a deterministic building block, with tests. Owner configuration
defines the allowed provider/model catalog and bounded retry delays; policy supplies
an ordered list of candidates for each task class. Selection distinguishes model
and provider limits, requires a probe after reset, never invents fallback models,
and waits when all candidates are limited. Authentication failures remain blocked
until explicitly updated. The caller must persist state and implement probes,
provider adapters and checkpoint continuation. No live model catalog is accepted
or inferred by this module.

The integration must replace specific Claude guarantees for both other providers:
secret isolation from tool subprocesses, offline command networking, write scopes,
ignored task-branch configuration/hooks, time/turn limits, usage accounting and
limit/reset parsing. Copilot output redaction alone is not credential isolation.
Do not arm the loop until these checks and the other setup topics are resolved.

## LabVIEW cloud runtime and version coverage

The local diagnostic found only one actual LabVIEW executable: 32-bit LabVIEW 2026
26.1.1f1, plus NI LabVIEW CLI. The CLI connected to LabVIEW and completed an operation
help request. A direct COM probe did not open an example successfully. These local
findings alone did not prove scripting or cloud operation; the hosted check below
now supplies separate cloud runtime evidence.
Directories named for older releases were not counted as installed editors.

The owner's expanded NI License Manager screenshot, supplied on 18 October 2026,
confirms LabVIEW 2026 Q1 Community Edition is Licensed until 27 June 2027.
Professional Development System is Unlicensed; Base, Full, Continuous Integration
and Debug Deployment show Evaluation Available, not active licenses. This screenshot
supersedes the earlier uncertainty from package metadata. It establishes local
Community activation, not activation of LabVIEW 2024 or a cloud machine. No
activation was changed and no private project, serial number or NI license file
was uploaded.

NI's Community usage guidance permits personal, non-commercial, non-industrial
projects and lists free open-source projects as an example. The owner explicitly
confirmed a private, non-commercial project on 18 October 2026. The public download page does not confirm authenticated
access to the 2024 installer. Native 2024 activation/execution remains unverified;
the selected official headless runtime does not require desktop activation for
its supported automation operations.

## Official NI cloud automation path

[NI's official container project](https://github.com/ni/labview-for-containers)
and [headless guide](https://github.com/ni/labview-for-containers/blob/2afb30b23bdb144368ee36d5f5ca33c06f800a98/docs/headless-labview.md)
provide a cloud automation path that does not need desktop activation for supported
non-development operations. The setup uses the owner's active Community development
license and confirmed personal use for a bounded analysis/build check. Applying
the development-license container terms to that combination is an interpretation
of the published terms, not a specific NI statement about this project. No paid-only
condition or explicit Community exclusion was found. See the
[NI agreement](https://www.ni.com/content/dam/web/pdfs/legal/software_license_agreement_en.pdf),
Addendum F, and [Community guidance](https://www.ni.com/en/support/documentation/supplemental/20/labview-community-edition-usage-details.html).

The container is for automation/analysis/testing; it must not be used to author or
edit LabVIEW source. No public LabVIEW service or redistributed container image is
created. The readiness workflow mounts only a disposable fixture directory, has
no model/account secrets, and disables container networking. It mass-compiles an
existing public MIT fixture and collects operation logs and package versions.
Compilation is an environment check, not product development or the benchmark.

Pins and input provenance live in `.github/loop/labview-runtime.json`; the public
workflow is `.github/workflows/labview-runtime.yml`. The image is NI's LabVIEW
2026 Q1 Linux release, pinned by digest. Its fixture comes from the pinned pylabview
LV2014 example and is SHA256-checked before use. Successful processing proves
that this runtime can load/compile that input; it does not prove semantic reading,
all-version compatibility, VI Scripting availability, or native LabVIEW 2024.

The official registry lists no LabVIEW 2024 image as of 18 October 2026. A separate
2024 installer/activation path remains to be investigated if native 2024 execution
is needed. Using the newer runtime for this setup check does not select the fallback
or change the owner's goal of all versions.

NI's published [software license agreement](https://www.ni.com/content/dam/web/pdfs/legal/software_license_agreement_en.pdf)
and [Community usage guidance](https://www.ni.com/en/support/documentation/supplemental/20/labview-community-edition-usage-details.html)
were used to assess the confirmed Community license and personal use. The cloud
baseline uses GitHub-hosted Ubuntu and the official headless image for analysis/build
automation under the interpretation stated above. No license or cloud VM purchase
was made, and no account activation or licensed local installation was transferred.

The environment baseline records tested public sources, a native cloud runtime,
account-access observations and known restrictions. It does not accept a new
product success gate. Shared availability, ordinary task adapters, credential
lifecycle recovery and continuation across limits belong to the owner-approved
multi-provider integration topic; its later implementation and verification are
recorded in [cloud authentication](cloud-authentication.md). Native 2024 execution,
all-version compatibility and full semantic reading remain unverified and must
not be reported as solved by this environment check.

The access/preparation topic was resolved with these explicit boundaries in
